question: What causal claim allows the speaker to assert knowledge of the Kaula determination in this address?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of the Kaulas.
The speaker claims to be known or to have come to know.
That knowledge is attributed to the grace of the addressed one.
The object of knowledge is the Kaula determination.
inference: By the grace of the lord of the Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the Kaula determination.
uncertainties: Ambiguity remains between jñāta as known and as one who has known.
plain_english: By your grace, O lord of the Kaulas, I have come to know the Kaula determination.
